So overall concept: Speech gives life and refines; importance of speech.

Option 2: "ز دل میار نسنجیده حرف را به زبان - عنان کشیده نگه دار اسب سرکش را". Means: From the heart bring unmeasured words to the tongue - keep a stretched rein on the wild horse. So: Speak from heart but control reckless speech? Actually first line: bring unmeasured words from heart to tongue. Second line: keep reins stretched on a wild horse (i.e., control). So concept: Speak freely but restrain? Could be about speech and restraint.

Option 3: "می فتد از پختگی بر خاک هر جا میوه ای است - جز سخنصائب که چون افتاد خامافتد به خاک". Means: From ripeness (maturity) fruit falls to the ground wherever there is fruit; except for speech (sokhan-saeeb?) that when it falls becomes raw on the ground? Something about speech being raw when it falls? So concept: Unlike fruit, speech becomes raw when it falls to ground. So maybe about speech being degraded when not used properly.

Option 4: "سخن دانِ پرورده پیر کهن - بیندیشی آنگاه بگوید سخن". Means: The word (speech) is nurtured by the old wise; think then speak. So concept: Speak after thinking, wisdom.
